newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha edges up, buoyed by European market.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha edges up, buoyed by European market.

text.p: Naphtha prices were a tad firmer on Wednesday despite overnight losses in crude oil prices, buttressed by the firmer European market, traders said.
Bids for second-half March open-spec naphtha were heard at $246.50, against notional offers at $248.00. It was assessed at $245.00/246.50 in late Tuesday trading.
First-half March was quoted at around $249.00/251.00, compared with Tuesday's levels at $248.25/250.00.
In spreads, first-half March/first-half April was discussed at plus $5.50/6.50 after it was traded twice at plus $6.25 and once at plus $6.00 on Tuesday.

Sentiment was said to have strengthened in the domestic low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market due to a fire on Monday at a desulphurisation unit at a refinery operated by Tohoku Oil, which is a Mitsubishi Oil group refiner.

Mitsubishi Oil said other group refineries would provide cargoes to Tohoku to cover production losses. But Mitsubishi Oil was rumoured to have asked some oil firms outside its group about their LSWR availability after the fire.
Whether the fire will lead to extra LSWR spot imports will depend on how long the unit remains shut, traders said.
